clue.text: Eager to join dishonest group

parts.note: sharp practice is dishonest dealing, so sharp can mean dishonest
a set is a group of things or people

explanation.surface: Someone keen to fall in with a crooked gang.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp-set is an old word for hungry, hence keen or avid.

clue.text: Become aware son is on American vessel

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
USS prefixes the names of United States Navy ships

explanation.surface: A parent realises their son is serving on a US warship.
explanation.definitionFit: To suss something is informal for working it out or realising it.

clue.text: A draft text containing nothing usable for book

indicators.note: containing means the draft text holds the nothing inside it

parts.note: MS is a manuscript, a draft text
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An early draft with nothing in it worth publishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is a book of the Old Testament, named for a prophet.

clue.text: Excuses as heads pin everything on one

indicators.note: pin means the heads word is pierced by the rest, holding it inside

parts.note: pates are heads

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the everything word above the one

parts.note: all means everything
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Excuses offered when bosses blame everything on one person.
explanation.definitionFit: To palliate a fault is to make it seem less serious, to extenuate it.

clue.text: Grovel, wrongly getting the universal blame, over confusion

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the rearranged letters above the last piece
wrongly means these letters are set out in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written
U is the film-classification letter for universal
taken as written
pie, printers' pie, is a jumble of type

explanation.surface: Someone unfairly taking the blame for a muddle and having to grovel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges THE U BLAME into EATHUMBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to apologise abjectly, to humble oneself.

clue.text: Press activity in closed court

definitions.meaning: the racket sport played in a walled indoor court

explanation.definitionFit: To squash is to crush flat; squash is also the racket game played inside four walls.

clue.text: To talk foolishly is rude for doctor

definitions.meaning: to chatter noisily and pointlessly, like a duck
an insulting word for a medical practitioner

explanation.walkthrough: 'rude for doctor' means a disrespectful name for a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A duck's cry gives a word for prattling, and a charlatan healer is a disparaging term for any physician.

clue.text: Is hesitant after organising opposition

indicators.note: after organising means the letters are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone holding back once an opposing faction is formed.
explanation.definitionFit: An antithesis is a direct contrast or opposite.

clue.text: Extensive financial assistance for such outstanding work

definitions.meaning: a generous level of state aid or tax concession
carving in which figures stand out far from the background

explanation.definitionFit: Generous aid could be called lavish help; in sculpture the term means carving projecting strongly from its ground.

clue.text: Writer's block limiting Defoe's creation

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing, so the block word goes round the creation

parts.note: a sett is a squared paving block
Moll Flanders is Daniel Defoe's heroine

explanation.surface: Writer's block stops a novelist finishing a Defoe pastiche.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer's block' reads as one phrase, but the writer is the definition and the block is a SETT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobias Smollett was an 18th-century Scottish novelist.

clue.text: Ordinary people providing paper with trite quotation

parts.note: rag is a dismissive word for a newspaper
a tag is a well-worn saying or quotation

explanation.surface: Common folk supplying a newspaper with a hackneyed quote.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragtag, as in ragtag and bobtail, is a scornful term for the common rabble.

clue.text: Nonchalant, risk catching bad cold around spring month

indicators.note: catching means the risk word holds everything else inside it

parts.note: to dare is to risk

indicators.note: around means the bad and cold words sit on either side of the month

parts.note: evil means bad
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
May is a month of spring

explanation.surface: A carefree type risks catching a bad cold in springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Devil-may-care describes a cheerfully reckless, unconcerned attitude.

clue.text: In freezing conditions, one may put eights on the river

definitions.text: In freezing conditions, one may put eights on the river

parts.words: In freezing conditions, one may put eights on the river
parts.note: eights sound like rowing crews on a river, but here they are figures of eight traced on a frozen river

explanation.surface: Rowing eights launched onto a river in winter.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer on ice traces figures such as eights with their blades.

clue.text: Bowl drained? In no state to take any more wallop

definitions.text: In no state to take any more wallop

parts.note: a bowl of punch, the mixed drink served at parties
a drink that has been drained has been drunk

explanation.surface: After emptying the punch bowl, someone can't face another beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Wallop is slang for beer, and also a heavy blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer dazed by too many blows can take no more punishment.

clue.text: Club house supporting a lot of weight

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting puts the house word underneath
a lot of means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: a stone is a British weight of fourteen pounds
a villa is a house

explanation.surface: A house built on a heavy foundation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' drops the last letter of STONE. A stone is 14 lb, a British weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Aston Villa is a Birmingham football club.

clue.text: Tip unusual result

definitions.meaning: a surprise win by the outsider in a contest

explanation.definitionFit: To upset is to knock over; an upset is also a shock result in sport.

clue.text: Good news shortly from wedding that creates a stir

parts.note: a terse telegram from a wedding would report on the bride
well means good, as in all is well

explanation.surface: A brief happy report from a wedding that causes excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a telegram: 'Bride well' is good news, sent briefly, from a wedding. Stir is slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridewell was a famous London jail, and its name became a general word for a prison, slang stir.

clue.text: In consequence, members of family were first to be fired

indicators.note: in means the family word goes inside the consequence word

parts.note: an end is an outcome or consequence
kin are relatives
led means were in front

explanation.surface: Relatives were the first to lose their jobs as a result.
explanation.definitionFit: To enkindle is to set alight, so enkindled means set on fire.

clue.text: Smile after vote that receives support from both sides

definitions.text: that receives support from both sides

indicators.note: after places the smile word behind the vote word

parts.note: voters mark a cross on the ballot paper
to beam is to smile broadly

explanation.surface: A grin after a ballot win that has backing from both parties.
explanation.definitionFit: A transverse timber is held up at each end by walls or posts.

clue.text: Sharp tool provided to cut joint, mostly

indicators.note: to cut into the joint means to go inside it
mostly means losing the last letter of the word

parts.note: the knee is a joint of the leg
provided means if, as in 'provided that'

explanation.surface: A sharp blade is needed to carve a joint of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade for cutting is the commonest sharp implement.

clue.text: Branching out, I'd turned to writing poetry

indicators.note: turned means the two letters of I'd are flipped around

parts.note: to versify is to write verse

explanation.surface: Someone explaining they widened their interests by taking up verse.
explanation.definitionFit: To diversify is to spread into new areas, like a business branching out.

clue.text: A page not even numbered?

parts.note: the right-hand page of a book, which always carries an odd number

explanation.surface: A page with no number on it at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The right-hand leaf of an open book carries odd page numbers.

clue.text: Clairvoyant's said to be disconcerting

definitions.note: the definition is a participle; the answer is the verb, with 'to be' joining

indicators.note: said means the word is spoken so its sound gives the answer

parts.note: fey can mean having second sight, so a clairvoyant is fey

explanation.surface: A psychic is reportedly unsettling.
explanation.definitionFit: To disturb or unsettle someone's composure, to throw them.

clue.text: Sally succeeded in boarding plane

indicators.note: boarding means getting on, so the succeeded letter goes into the plane

parts.note: a jet is a plane

explanation.surface: Sally made it onto the aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a witty remark or quip.

clue.text: For free, shave head?

definitions.meaning: to take off all one's locks of hair

explanation.surface: Someone getting a head shave at no cost.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: removing your locks is to un-lock.
explanation.definitionFit: To unlock is to set free; whimsically, it also means losing one's locks of hair.

clue.text: Avoiding fatality by discontinuing operation?

parts.note: a system designed so that when it breaks down it stops in a harmless state

explanation.surface: A surgeon calling off an operation to save a life.
explanation.definitionFit: A design whose breakdown mode is harmless shuts down rather than causing disaster.

clue.text: Monarch careless over source of warning signal

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king
lax means slack or careless
on can mean over, as in a lid on a pot

explanation.surface: A negligent king ignoring the origin of an alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud electric horn, once fitted to cars, that sounds an alert.

clue.text: Result of runners doing their level best?

definitions.text: Result of runners doing their level best?

parts.words: Result of runners doing their level best?
parts.note: level best usually means maximum effort, but here the runners finish exactly level

explanation.surface: Athletes all trying as hard as they can.
explanation.definitionFit: A race finish in which two competitors cannot be separated.
